No: she was told she was the help back in Genesis 2; Genesis 3:16 confirms the rule after the transgression. So why do we feel today that being a help is a bad thing?
precepts.point: Brothers, the same goes the other way: the moment you decide not to provide, not to be the man God told you to be, watch what happens to your household. It is a domino effect. Some of you brothers did not want a wife; you wanted a mama.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“I will make him an help meet for him.” To help is to give assistance or support to someone, to provide something useful or necessary in achieving an end. Meet means suitable for him. So the help is the one who assists in making what the husband wants happen. Sometimes the help thinks she is supposed to lead, or thinks she is supposed to guide, but that is not what a help is.

Genesis 3:16 comes after the transgression: “thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” Some have taken this to mean it was only at this point that the woman was supposed to listen to her husband. No. She was told she was the help back in Genesis 2; Genesis 3:16 confirms the rule after the fall.

So why do we feel today that being a help is a bad thing? Sisters, the help is the greatest thing you are ever going to be. The moment you decide being the help is not the greatest thing you can be, or think you are supposed to be something outside of the help, you are going to destroy your marriage.

It cuts both ways. Brothers, the moment you decide not to provide, not to leave the house and work, not to be the man God told you to be, watch what happens to your household: your marriage will crumble and your life will be in shambles. It is a domino effect. And headship is maintenance, a routine thing a husband has to keep doing. A wife will never say she is trying to overthrow you, but it is in her spirit, the same way a man wants to do things his own way when he gets orders from those ranked above him. So you will have to remind her: I am the head, you have to listen to me.

precepts.text: In the scriptures the Most High compares men to beasts: that they might see that they themselves are beasts. So the serpent in Genesis 3 is a representation of a man.
precepts.point: She took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, because she was persuaded by the serpent, and then she gave to her husband, and he did eat. The serpent did not use force; he used words to sway Eve's perception of reality, and then she went into sin. The serpent went to the woman first; that is why the apostles taught that the woman is to learn from her husband at home.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
“Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.” The serpent is counted among the beasts, and in the scriptures the Most High compares men to beasts. Solomon wrote, “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” So the serpent in Genesis 3 is a representation of a man.

He was more subtle than any beast: more crafty, better with his lies, better with his persuasion. Satan’s first weapon was persuasion. Eve was not subdued physically; he did not grab her. He came to her with words. “Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” Notice what he brings: doubt and fear. Eve answered correctly, that God had said “Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.” Then came the doubt: “Ye shall not surely die,” and “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” She was already meant to be eternal, but he threw doubt in to persuade her to eat.

“she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.” She was persuaded by the serpent, and then she defiled Adam as well. The serpent used no force; he used words to sway Eve’s perception of reality, and then she went into sin. He went to the woman first, which is why the woman is to learn from her husband at home.

That same serpent spirit is still speaking. Christ told the Pharisees, “Ye are of your father the devil,” “a liar, and the father of it.” The serpent seed came through Cain, and it lives on in Esau, the so-called white man, the pioneer of lying, who persuades the world today through his media and his religion. It is a battle for the minds of the people, and the answer is to stay in the word.

precepts.why:
“Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.” That don't mean they were butt naked and needed clothes. It means God gave them a way to get forgiveness of their sin. Animal sacrifice was introduced right here, in Genesis 3:21: God clothed them with righteousness and forgiveness.

That is the key to Genesis 4. Cain “brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.” Abel “brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof.” “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering”, because Abel's offering was in accordance with Genesis 3:21. Cain did not roll that way. He decided he was not going to do what God said and brought fruits and vegetables instead.

“But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” His countenance falling means he got mad. He got pissed off. God asked him, “Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” and told him, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Doing well was obeying what God had set in place; sin lying at the door was disobedience.

So the difference between Cain and Abel was not the gift; it was obedience. Abel followed the way God had already shown his parents, and Cain replaced it with his own way. That disobedience is where Cain's line started.

precepts.point: If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold. They did not just kill the one man that hurt Lamech; they wiped out that whole lineage. That is how Esau gets down; remember who their desire was to.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
God said to Cain, “And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” This is a parable. God is speaking about the spiritual demon, Satan: the “thee” is Satan, and it is Cain's desire that would be unto him.

To see the pattern, go back to Genesis 3:16. “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” If a woman desires anything, whether it is sex, wisdom, knowledge or money, it must be to her husband, and he rules over her.

Read Genesis 4:7 with that in mind. Just as a woman's desire is to her husband, Cain's desire would be to Satan. Anything Cain wanted, he would have to go to Satan for it, and Satan would rule over him.

So Satan was over Cain and over his seed. When we read about Cain's children, the city, the cattle, the music, the weapons and Lamech's vengeance, we should not read them as holy and righteous. This is Cain's seed, and their desire is always unto Satan.

precepts.text: His hand hath formed the crooked serpent. God formed Satan.
precepts.point: The serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field, which the Lord God had made. The serpent is Satan, called a serpent because he is slick and forked-tongued, and God made him exactly as subtil as he is.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.why:
When did the war start? Through the envy of the devil, when he made his move on Adam’s kingdom. And he made that move through Adam’s wife: “Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.”

The serpent is Satan, the devil. It says serpent, but it is not talking about a snake; he is called a serpent because he is slick, forked-tongued, tricky. And notice, “which the Lord God had made.” God created him to be exactly who he is. He was subtil because God made him subtil.

Job confirms it: “By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.” God formed that crooked serpent, Satan. He is not a rival power that rose up on his own to equal God; he is a creature God made, crooked by design.

So Satan tricked Eve, the weaker vessel, and caused her to sin, and Eve went and convinced her husband to sin. Then the Most High came to deal with Adam, Eve and Satan, and brought judgment on all three. From there God declared the war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”.

That is why we have to know our adversary. The serpent that deceived Eve is the same one we fight today, in his whispers and in his children, and the one who formed him is the one who will judge him.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.why:
Satan made his move on Adam through the weaker vessel, and God brought judgment on the serpent, the woman and the man. To the serpent: “Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field”. That is not about livestock. This is paradise; he is cursed above every creation God made there. And, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”.

That one line says two things. Man was made from the earth, and Satan is a celestial being, so “all the days of thy life” means his days are numbered: he will be destroyed in the future for what he did. And eating dust means he is on the earth, and the Lord handed him power over it.

Luke shows it: “the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” When was the power of this earth delivered to Satan? In Genesis 3, what we just read.

And he gave it to whom he would: first to Cain, and then to Esau, the so-called white man in these last days. That is why Esau is able to create all this technology.

Then comes the declaration of war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Back then her seed was Abel, then Seth and the chosen lineage, and Satan’s seed was Cain and his descendants. Today her seed is the twelve tribes of Israel, and his seed is the so-called Caucasians, Edom. And “it shall bruise thy head”, because his seed, the Romans, crucified Christ. Then, “and thou shalt bruise his heel”: the Lord will take down Satan and his children. So when the Bible says to be soldiers of Jesus Christ, we fight Satan, his wicked thoughts and whispers, and we also fight his children, his physical counterpart.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.why:
“Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.” Satan does not run around doing his own thing. He goes before the Lord and answers to him.

“And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” That walking up and down in the earth is the dust he eats. In Genesis 3 God said, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”. Here is that judgment being lived out: his job is to walk the earth to see whom he can tempt and destroy. Satan became the tempter, and that is his judgment; soon he will be destroyed.

It happened after Satan was judged, and it shows the order of things. The power of this world was delivered to him, but he still presents himself before the Lord and reports where he has been.

The word Satan comes from a Hebrew term meaning adversary: accuser, opponent. And the word devil means deceiver. He is the Lord’s adversary and our adversary. And not only the spiritual Satan: his seed, his children, are our adversary too, because God put enmity between his seed and her seed. The so-called white man is our adversary, and the spiritual demon Satan is our adversary. That is the war we are in.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
In the garden, before Adam and Eve were put out, God said, “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Enmity is hatred. Satan has seed on this earth, and the woman’s seed, the descendants who would come through her, is Israel. When that was spoken, Cain was not yet born. The seed of Satan was Cain.

Genesis 4 shows how. “And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” If you obey me, will you not be accepted by me? But “and if thou doest not well”, if you choose to break my commandments, “sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” The one spoken of there is Satan: Satan would be Cain’s desire, and would rule over him. Satan would be Cain’s god and Cain’s father.

Cain chose not to obey, and he killed Abel. From that moment the enmity of Genesis 3:15 was at work in the earth: the seed of the serpent against the seed of the woman.

It did not end with Cain. His line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau, the one who “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob, whose hand took hold on Esau’s heel. So Genesis 3:15 and Genesis 4:7 explain the hatred Edom has for Israel to this day: it is the enmity God put between the two seeds in the beginning.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
“And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Don’t you see something wrong there? Abel was already dead, and Cain was still alive. So why does it never say that Cain was in Adam’s image?

Go back to the making of Adam: “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle”. Adam, the black man, was made in the image of God. Adam and Eve had Cain and Abel; Cain killed Abel, because God had told him that if he did not do well, sin lay at the door and Satan would rule over him.

Then, when it names the son born “in his own likeness, after his image”, it names Seth, not Cain. People say everybody is in the image of God. No: Cain was not in the image of God, and he is never said to be in Adam’s image.

So whose image was Cain in? John answers it: Cain “was of that wicked one”. Seth was of Adam; Cain was of Satan. That is why the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent are two different seeds, and why Seth’s line, the line that returns as Jacob, is the one that carries Adam’s image.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil”. There are children of God on the planet, and there are children of the devil on the planet. And “whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another”.

“Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Wait: we thought Cain was of Adam. It says no. Seth was of Adam; Cain was of that wicked one, of Satan. That is exactly what God told Cain in Genesis 4: unto thee shall be his desire, and he shall rule over thee. “And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.”

This is the enmity of Genesis 3:15 made plain: “between thy seed and her seed”. Satan’s seed is Cain, the children of the devil, and her seed is Israel, the children of God.

Cain’s line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau, and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob. Esau “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, and Idumea, the Greek and Roman name for Edom, is that same Esau. So when we ask who the children of the devil are in the earth today and why they hate us, John has already told us: not as Cain, who was of that wicked one.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Paul speaks of the man of sin: “Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”. His coming is after the working of Satan, meaning Satan is his father, as he was Cain’s. That is Esau, Cain come again.

Genesis 3:15 ends, “it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.” Christ is our head, smitten so that the sheep were scattered. But the heel is Edom’s Achilles heel. Jacob took hold of Esau’s heel at birth, and in Daniel 2 “a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces.”

The image is the empires. The head of gold is Nebuchadnezzar and Babylon; the silver is Persia and Media; the brass is Greece, “which shall bear rule over all the earth.” That was Alexander, “son of Philip, the Macedonian”, who “slew the kings of the earth” until “the earth was quiet before him; whereupon he was exalted and his heart was lifted up”: the beginning of white supremacy in the earth. His kingdom was parted among his generals, “and evils were multiplied in the earth.” Their own books, The Chronology of Ancient Nations and The Rise of Christendom, trace Philip back to Esau. The iron is Rome, and we are still in it: America and NATO, a kingdom “partly strong, and partly broken”, strong in military, with the toes as the European nations. The miry clay is the melting pot: “they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another”.

The stone is Christ, “Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. He strikes the image on its feet, its heel, and “the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.” And “in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people”. We are living in the days of these kings. What we teach is the beginning of that kingdom, and it cannot be stopped; it will consume all these kingdoms with the word of God.

note.label: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.why:
“And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?” Where are you, Adam? I put you down here to rule this earth, and now I'm looking for you. “And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked”. He was afraid because he knew he had messed up. Naked means exposed to sin. They were not running around without clothes; they were never supposed to have the knowledge of sin, and now sin was in them. And Satan showed it to Eve first.

To show what Satan did, the class read how he tempted Christ, from Luke 4. Christ was “led by the Spirit into the wilderness, Being forty days tempted of the devil.” That is what brothers are going to go through: you will be tempted, and a man is supposed to be able to resist temptation. Women are not as strong as men, which is why she is supposed to look up to you. Christ resisted.

First the bread: “If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread.” You have the power, so why sit here hungry? It was an attempt to make Christ forget why he was fasting, the way a cupboard full of food tempts you to forget your purpose. “It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.” Women will forget the course they are on, and that is why men have to protect her. She is in serious trouble without a husband.

Then Satan raised the stakes: “And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” That is what Satan did to Eve. He likely hit her several times while she resisted, and then showed her something greater: you do not have to be under your husband; a time will come when you will be over him. He showed her America, with the man serving her, selling drugs for her, committing crimes for her, worshipping her. She spiritually fornicated with Satan, and brought it back to Adam with her beauty, without telling him about the death, and he took the bait.

When the reckoning came, Adam blamed her: “The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.” It was not her fault; God put him over her, and Adam did not have to listen. Then she blamed the serpent: “The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.” The family unit was attacked. The family is the backbone of the nation, and once husband and wife violate each other's roles they work against each other instead of for each other, and the children come out confused and troubled. That destruction came down through the generations to husbands and wives today. Men must restore the order and bring back our civility.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Genesis 3:20 is right there in front of our eyes: “And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.” She was the mother, bringing forth many children. This was before she fell and before Adam was cast out. The living are children on the earth, created before the fall, and Eve was the mother of them all. Eve was a black woman and she was beautiful. That was Adam and Eve in their kingdom, not people walking around naked.

2 Esdras 3 shows how many there were: “And unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” When Adam broke God's law he was cast out of paradise and immortality was taken from him. But there were already nations, tribes, people and kindreds, out of number, so many they could not be counted. For all of that to be around, Adam must have been on the earth for hundreds or thousands of years.

2 Esdras 6:54: “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures”. Adam was a lord on the earth, ruling the earth and the heavens. The creatures include the angels, and Adam was over them. “of him come we all”. The words “and the people also whom thou hast chosen” were read as speaking of after the flood, from Noah, because before Noah, and before Adam fell, there were people already. And verse 55: “thou madest the world for our sakes”.

That is how Cain was able to find a wife after he killed Abel. There were many people living on the earth, tribes and nations, and Adam was governing them all. And he was not alone: we were with him in the beginning, the twelve tribes, ruling the heavens and the earth with him. What we read about the future kingdom, governing the nations in angelic bodies, is how it was with Adam. Tobit 8:6 says of Adam and Eve, “of them came mankind”, but that is broad, since all mankind also came from Adam and Eve through Noah's three sons.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
Chapter 3 deals with the craftiness of your enemy, and the first thing to settle is who the serpent is. This is not a literal snake; serpents do not speak. Another word for serpent is deceiver, and the serpent is Satan.

“And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.” Satan transforms himself; he comes in disguise. So the serpent “more subtil than any beast of the field” that spoke to the woman is Satan in disguise, and his first words show the craft: “Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?”

precepts.text: The fruit of lies is eaten; the fruit Eve ate was the lie she was taught.
precepts.point: The fruit she ate was the lies. She was enticed to break the commandments of the Most High, then she went and taught her husband the same thing the serpent taught her, and he broke the commandments as well.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“Ye have plowed wickedness, ye have reaped iniquity; ye have eaten the fruit of lies”. Fruit is eaten, and here the fruit eaten is lies. Any time scripture speaks of good for food like this, it is talking about good to learn.

So the fruit Eve ate was the lies. The woman saw that the tree “was good for food”, “pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise”: she was enticed to break the commandments of the Most High. Then she “gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat”: she went and taught her husband the same thing the serpent taught her, and he broke the commandments as well.

precepts.text: Adam covered his transgressions; the fig leaves are that covering.
precepts.point: Remember this is an illustrated story. The fig leaves and aprons represent them trying to cover their transgressions.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom”. Adam covered his transgressions. That is what the fig leaves are.

Remember this is an illustrated story. When “they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons”, the fig leaves and aprons represent them trying to cover their transgressions, hiding their iniquity as Adam did.

precepts.text: Jerusalem sinned and her nakedness was seen; nakedness is sin.
precepts.point: Remember this is an illustrated story. The fig leaves and aprons represent them trying to cover their transgressions.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“Jerusalem hath grievously sinned; therefore she is removed: all that honoured her despise her, because they have seen her nakedness”. Jerusalem sinned, and what was seen was her nakedness. Nakedness is sin.

So when “the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked”, they were not literally naked. They knew they were in sin, and the fig leaf aprons were their attempt to cover the transgression.

precepts.text: The trees in the garden of God are men among whom a man may seek to hide.
precepts.point: The trees of the garden here are people. Adam and his wife tried to hide their sins among the other people that were in the garden with them.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him: the fir trees were not like his boughs, and the chesnut trees were not like his branches; nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty.” The trees in the garden of God are men, and a man may seek to hide among them.

That is what Adam and his wife did. The trees of the garden here are people, and when they “hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God amongst the trees of the garden”, they were trying to hide their sins among the other people that were in the garden with them.

precepts.text: The nations lick up the dust, showing the low estate spoken to the serpent.
precepts.point: Going on the belly and eating dust means the serpent was brought to a very low estate, made like a vagabond upon the earth. Cain became a vagabond upon the earth, and so did Esau.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers: they shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet”. The kings and queens of the nations are brought down to lick the dust at Israel's feet: a very low estate.

That is the estate spoken to the serpent: “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”. Going on the belly and eating dust means being brought very low, made like a vagabond upon the earth. Cain became a vagabond upon the earth, and so did Esau.

precepts.text: The nations shall lick the dust like a serpent, proving the cattle and beasts are the nations.
precepts.point: Going on the belly and eating dust means the serpent was brought to a very low estate, made like a vagabond upon the earth. Cain became a vagabond upon the earth, and so did Esau.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“The nations shall see and be confounded at all their might: they shall lay their hand upon their mouth, their ears shall be deaf. They shall lick the dust like a serpent, they shall move out of their holes like worms of the earth”. The nations lick the dust like a serpent.

That proves who the cattle and the beasts of the field are in the curse, “thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field”: the cattle and the beasts are the nations. And licking the dust is the low estate of the serpent's curse, being made like a vagabond upon the earth, as Cain became a vagabond and Esau after him.

precepts.text: The sons of men are themselves called beasts.
precepts.point: Going on the belly and eating dust means the serpent was brought to a very low estate, made like a vagabond upon the earth. Cain became a vagabond upon the earth, and so did Esau.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” The sons of men are themselves called beasts.

So when the serpent is “cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field”, the beasts are not animals: they are the nations, the sons of men. The serpent, Satan, is cursed above them all.

precepts.text: The Most High speaks to Israel as the woman.
precepts.point: It shall bruise thy head is spoken to the serpent: Christ was going to come and destroy the works of Satan.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“Lift up thine eyes unto the high places, and see where thou hast not been lien with. In the ways hast thou sat for them, as the Arabian in the wilderness; and thou hast polluted the land with thy whoredoms and with thy wickedness.” The Most High is speaking to Israel, and He speaks to her as the woman.

That shows who the woman is in Genesis 3:15. This is a prophecy, not the serpent and Eve: the woman is the nation of Israel. And the woman does not plant seed, the man plants seed, so the Most High is saying He will put enmity between Satan's seed and Israel's seed, and that enmity remains. Christ was to come from the woman, and Revelation 12 explains this verse.

Bruising the heel is making Israel stumble. When a serpent strikes at your heel you stumble; Satan makes Israel stumble through evil communication and corrupting good manners.

precepts.text: The Most High bruises Satan under the feet of His people; that is the bruising of the head.
precepts.point: It shall bruise thy head is spoken to the serpent: Christ was going to come and destroy the works of Satan.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.” The Most High bruises Satan under the feet of His people. That is the bruising of the head.

“it shall bruise thy head” is spoken to the serpent: Christ was going to come and destroy the works of Satan. Satan bruises the heel, making Israel stumble; Christ bruises the head, and Satan goes under the feet of Israel.

precepts.text: The women are commanded to be under obedience, as the law says from the beginning.
precepts.point: Sisters, if you do not allow your husband to rule over you, it does not matter what else you keep; you are not entering the kingdom without fulfilling this.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law.” The women are commanded to be under obedience, and Paul points back to the law for it, because the law says it from the beginning.

The beginning is Genesis 3:16: “thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” Your desire, your learning, your desire of anything was to be to your husband, and he shall rule over thee. It is one of the first commandments given, alongside be fruitful and multiply, the Sabbath, and the commandment not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

Sisters, if you do not allow your husband to rule over you, it does not matter what else you keep; you are not entering the kingdom without fulfilling this.

precepts.text: The Most High clothes His saints with righteousness, as Adam was clothed to cover sin.
precepts.point: The first sacrifice is twofold. A literal lamb was slain here to clothe Adam and his wife, and that lamb slain from the foundation of the world represents Christ, slain for our sins.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness”. The Most High clothes His saints with righteousness; He covers them.

That is what the coats of skins were about. When the Lord God made “coats of skins, and clothed them”, it was a covering for sin: animal sacrifice to cover the sins of Adam and his wife. As Adam was clothed to cover sin, the saints are clothed and covered with righteousness.

precepts.text: The sin offering yields skins, as the Most High made coats of skins to cover sin.
precepts.point: The first sacrifice is twofold. A literal lamb was slain here to clothe Adam and his wife, and that lamb slain from the foundation of the world represents Christ, slain for our sins.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“And the bullock for the sin offering, and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, shall one carry forth without the camp; and they shall burn in the fire their skins, and their flesh, and their dung.” The sin offering yields skins.

So when the Lord God made Adam and his wife “coats of skins”, an animal had been slain for sin. This is where the Most High ordained the sacrificial law; this is when they started to sacrifice, and the skins that covered them came from a sacrifice for their sin.

precepts.text: The Lamb was slain from the foundation of the world; Christ is that Lamb.
precepts.point: The first sacrifice is twofold. A literal lamb was slain here to clothe Adam and his wife, and that lamb slain from the foundation of the world represents Christ, slain for our sins.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” Christ is that Lamb.

The first sacrifice is twofold. A literal lamb was slain here, at the foundation of the world, to make the coats of skins that clothed Adam and his wife and covered their sin; and that lamb slain from the foundation of the world represents Christ, slain for our sins. The sacrificial law ordained in the garden points to Him from its first day.

precepts.text: The coats of skins were the first sacrifice; the beast stood in place of Adam and Eve.
precepts.point: That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from Genesis 3.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“at the hand of every beast will I require it”: the Most High requiring blood at the hand of every beast is animal sacrifice, still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation. It begins in Genesis 3. “Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.” Those coats of skins were the first sacrifice.

The judgment for sin has always been death. When Eve sinned and caused Adam to sin, either they had to die, or something had to stand in their place. The beast whose skin clothed them stood in for Adam and Eve; the blood of the animal stood in for them.

precepts.text: Enmity is set between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed; the battle between Esau's seed and Israel stands until the end.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
The war with Amalek from generation to generation is older than Amalek. In the garden the Lord said, “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.” The enmity was set between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed from the beginning.

The battle between Esau's seed and Israel is that enmity, and it stands until the end. They bruised Christ's heel. But the head is bruised at the end of the world, and it is Jacob who bruises it. What Amalek began against the feeble and the weary coming out of Egypt is the serpent's seed against the woman's seed, and it ends the way the garden said it would.

precepts.text: Thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.
precepts.point: The war laws give the same understanding: the man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her was sent back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her, for the Lord is the one that goeth with the host to fight against the enemies.

note.label: Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor

precepts.why:
“When a man hath taken a new wife, he shall not go out to war, neither shall he be charged with any business: but he shall be free at home one year, and shall cheer up his wife which he hath taken.” Make it plain: the first year, stay at home and make a baby.

Genesis lays the ground of the marriage he stays home for: “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” Her desire is to her husband, and he rules over her; the year free at home is given to that.

precepts.text: The seed of the woman that should bruise the serpent's head.
precepts.point: What he came to fulfil is the prophecies written concerning him, not the commandments given to Israel to keep. Everything in chapter 2 of this same gospel is an example of that fulfilling.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
The first prophecy Christ came to fulfil is in the law of Moses, in the garden: “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.”

Christ is the seed of the woman that should bruise the serpent's head. This was written concerning him, and it is the kind of thing he meant when he said he came to fulfil the law and the prophets.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why: Who is Adam? “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” Adam was the son of God. So when we read that Jesus Christ was the son of God, the apostles understood all that meant: that he is Adam, literally the son of God. He was made flesh in Genesis, and he was made flesh in the time of the apostles.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why:
“Yet it pleased the Lord to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin”. The him here is Christ, Adam. Remember what the Lord said in the beginning: it shall bruise thy head. This is Adam being bruised. His soul made an offering for sin: that is atonement.

Read back in the chapter: “He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief”. Christ was hated. “Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.” That is Christ.

And on: “by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities.” That is atonement: the prophecy of Adam, Christ, coming and dying and bearing our iniquities.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why: “Will the Lord be pleased with thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of rivers of oil? shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?” This is all talking about Adam, the son of God, coming and dying: the firstborn given for the transgression.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why:
“For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.” This goes back to Genesis 3:15, Micah 6:7 and Isaiah 53: it pleased the Lord to bruise him, when he made his soul an offering for sin.

Through Adam everybody died. Then Adam came back, walked perfectly, and fixed it, and we are all going to live. He came, died and sacrificed himself for us; he became that atonement for us. That is our head being bruised.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why: “For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.” Christ knew no sin, yet he was made to be sin for us. He became that sacrifice for us.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why:
“For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God”. He was perfect, but he suffered for our sins. He was just, and he suffered for the unjust, and the unjust is us.

“Being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit”. The Lord brought him back to life. He was put to death in the flesh and came back in the spirit; he changed, because he walked perfect. “By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison”.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why:
“Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus”. That is how we get redemption.

“Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past”. Propitiation is a covering, an atoning sacrifice. He is our atoning and our sacrifice. On this day we celebrate that Christ is our atonement; the sacrifices we did all the time were always a representation of Christ.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why: “And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous”. An advocate is a lawyer: if you sin, you have a lawyer. “And he is the propitiation for our sins”: he is the atonement for our sins. That is how we get atonement, through Christ.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why:
“Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.” Propitiation means atonement: he sent his son to be the atonement for our sin.

“Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another.” We are to love one another.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 7 Sealing The 144k

precepts.why: This is what being saved in childbearing goes back to, a verse many American women despise. “In sorrow thou shalt bring forth children”: the childbearing pains, and the cramps every month. “And thy desire shall be to thy husband”: this is the desire you women must have to be saved. “And he shall rule over thee”: that’s the judgment. Childbearing doesn’t just mean having babies; she remembers why she suffers the pains, for being disobedient to the Lord.

note.label: | Explaining Dark Sentences | Part 3

precepts.why:
Men, pay attention; I’m dealing with the women right now. “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow”: this is going into her menstrual cycle and her labour pains. “And thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.”

Why does the woman have pains during childbirth, and cramps and things like that? Because of sin. And Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. So in the kingdom, is she going to have menstrual cycles and cramps and all that? No. That’s going to be over. You women need to clap for that day.

note.label: RACIAL IDOLATRY: RACISM & PATRIOTISM

precepts.why: “Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner.” The godly is Jacob; the sinner is Esau, the wicked. God set good against evil, and that is why these people hate us so much.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: Who does Eve represent? “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.” So Eve in Genesis represents Israel: the woman, the woman, the woman. That thought does not change through the rest of the class.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: “Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel’s furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not.” Rachel had stolen her father’s gods and hid them. “And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women is upon me.” Rachel told her father, I can’t get up, I’m unclean right now, I’m on my menstrual, and she hid the gods around her. What custom is that? Go back to Genesis 3:16: the woman’s sorrow.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: The law shows what her sorrow is. “And if a woman have an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she shall be put apart seven days”. Her issue is her menstrual, and she is put apart seven days. Remember the thought has not changed: Eve is symbolic of the woman in Jeremiah 6:2, Israel.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
Watch what it calls it here. “And if a man shall lie with a woman having her sickness”: her sickness is her menstrual, her issue, her sorrow. “And shall uncover her nakedness; he hath discovered her fountain, and she hath uncovered the fountain of her blood: and both of them shall be cut off from among their people.” He laid with her during her menstrual, he gets death and so does she. It is unclean, an abomination, to lie with your woman in the midst of her sickness, her sorrow, her issue of blood. Do not run the red light; it’s nasty.

Menstrual means relating to the menses, and menses in the Latin means month, because her sickness comes monthly, a monthly cycle where the body cleans itself out. Menstrual goes back to the word month: her month of sorrow, her month of sickness, her month of issue. And by law it lasts seven days.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
“If a woman have conceived seed, and born a man child: then she shall be unclean seven days; according to the days of the separation for her infirmity shall she be unclean.” “And in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.” After the seven days, on the eighth day, she is officially clean: at the seventh day’s sundown she is clean, she takes the man child to the temple, they both are purified and offer sacrifices, and the male child is circumcised on the eighth day, making him clean. They both become clean on the eighth day.

“And she shall then continue in the blood of her purifying three and thirty days”: she has more impurity for the next 33 days, 40 days in all for a boy, and you can’t lie with her for that time; she has to heal. So: unclean seven days, the child circumcised and clean the eighth day.

note.label: | SABBATH EVENING CLASS: Our Salvation & China's Desolation

precepts.why: “And he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life”: to keep the way of the truth. These cherubims, these angelic spirits, their job was to block the way of truth.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 19 Supper, War & Marriage

precepts.why: Why the wedding garment is heavy. Satan is talking to the woman, Eve. “And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food”: this tree represented idolatry, philosophies. “She took of the fruit thereof”: she learned it, she studied it. “And gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat”: she taught him. Eve learned something from the devil, went to her husband, usurped his authority, and said this is the real deal. That happens on a lot of levels today: the brothers will be trying to get themselves right, and then the woman brings her philosophy to him, and next thing you know he’s following the wife in evil instead of the Most High. “And the eyes of them both were opened”: their spiritual understanding. “And they knew that they were naked.” “And they sewed fig leaves together”: that’s for another class, where they tried to hide amongst the nations and be like the nations.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 19 Supper, War & Marriage

precepts.why: “Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them”: the coats of skin go into the righteousness, which represents the law. What law gave them forgiveness for the sins they committed? Sacrifice. It’s not talking about them literally being naked here.

note.label: | SABBATH EVENING CLASS: War In Heaven And In Earth

precepts.why:
Still dealing with the pain, the value and the gift of pain. “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children”: screaming and hollering, pain, pain, pain. It wasn’t supposed to be like this. Every time she has a baby it is a constant reminder of her disobedience against her husband. But he goes to the medical field for painkillers and epidurals so she doesn’t feel it, and she never understands the value of why God gave the pain, which lets her continue to be disobedient to her husband, and that abscess, that toothache, is going to be her death.

“And thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee”: that is what the pain is supposed to remind her of. The Bishop rightly pointed out, and he should know with twelve or fourteen children, that a woman in childbirth is in the most vulnerable position of her whole existence. There ain’t a damn thing she can do if the house catches on fire; she has to be there until it’s finished. God gave that excruciating pain to remind her of the Commandment to obey her husband, and “she shall be saved in childbearing” because in that childbearing she is supposed to remember this.

“And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife”: it was supposed to be him teaching her, but she ended up teaching him, usurping authority over him, and that’s out of order with the Lord. So the Lord gave him pain to remember: “cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life.” “Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee”, “In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground”: work, work, work, when it was given to us in the beginning; until you die. Every time we work it is a reminder that we should not be listening to our wives.

Men need time to think on manly stuff and keep their minds on war, trying to get the kingdom, not carried off into conversations that most of the time ain’t righteous. That doesn’t mean she can’t say nothing; when she comes with scripture, she can speak.

“And Adam called his wife’s name Eve”: he named her, he got his sense back after getting that butt whipping from the Most High. “Because she was the mother of all living”: everybody came from her, Cain and Abel and all the rest of the people.

“Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them”: that is when the law of sacrifice was introduced. The coats of skins are talking about the animals, and the very next chapter proves it.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why: The law of sacrifice was instituted during the time of Adam and Eve. “Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.” The coats of skins were to cover them from their sins. That is a parable, a metaphor: it is talking about animal sacrifice. How do we know it is talking about sacrifice? Genesis 4:4: Abel knew to bring of the firstlings of his flock because animal sacrifice was introduced right here. The blood of the animal gave, at that time, the forgiveness of sin.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

precepts.why:
“For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life. For neither were they from the beginning, neither shall they be for ever. For by the vain glory of men they entered into the world, and therefore shall they come shortly to an end.”

Idol worship was the beginning. Think about it: if you do something other than what God told you to do, what god did you follow to do it? It is a god, an idol, somebody or something you put above the Lord, whether it is yourself, your own mind, or somebody telling you something. At that point you figured they had more power and you should go the direction they said. That is idol worship, and that was the beginning of it all.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

precepts.why: “For the worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil.” The beginning was the worship of idols. Eve put something before God, whether herself or somebody else, and she brought it to her husband.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

precepts.why:
“Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned.” When this took place it fell on all men. Notice it still says by one man: the one being charged with the offense is the man, Adam, because he was the head and was supposed to instruct his household.

He is the head of his household, therefore he is responsible. Brothers, when your wife does something stupid, we are looking at you. When your kids are out of order, when your house is jacked up, we are looking at you. We haven't forgotten about the wife, but who is ultimately the cause? Your leadership is failing somewhere. So are you going to fix it, or whine about it: that's the woman you gave me?

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

precepts.why:
“When Adam transgressed my statutes, then was decreed that now is done.” When Adam transgressed, things were made the way they are now. Above this Ezra speaks of the dangers of reaching the glorious, beautiful city and the beautiful sea: to get there you have to go through a narrow path, the only way, and a dangerous road. You didn't have these problems when you were in the world; it turns up when you come into this truth.

“And that the glory of the most High is kept to defend them which have led a wary life, whereas we have walked in the most wicked ways of all?” Ezra was righteous, but he was real about himself, and he equates himself with those who fall short. points: Because Adam hearkened to his wife and broke the commandment, the ground was cursed for his sake; in sorrow and sweat he would eat of it all his days.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

points: The man was driven out of the garden to till the ground from whence he was taken, and the way of the tree of life was kept.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

points: This is the prophecy of Christ being our atonement. “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman”. Enmity is hatred, between Satan and the woman. “And between thy seed and her seed”: Satan’s seed, which is Esau, and her seed, which is Israel. That is good against evil.

Because he sinned, sin came in and we all have to die; so Adam came and fixed that mistake. This is God prophesying Adam, the son of God, coming and dying for our sins.

“And thou shalt bruise his heel.” Adam is going to take down Satan and his children. Jacob grabbed hold of Esau’s heel; that represents Adam destroying the devil and his children. That is what we are waiting on right now: for our king to return and take them down by their heel.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

God put enmity there, so there will always be a conflict and a fight between good and evil, between Jacob and Esau, between Cain and Abel, between blacks and Caucasians. If you have asked yourself why these people hate you so much, it is because God set good against evil. “It shall bruise thy head.”

note.label: RACIAL IDOLATRY: RACISM & PATRIOTISM

Between Israel and Satan’s children, Edom, there will be war, and we are at war.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow”: thy sorrow is the menstruation, the bleeding every month, the cramps. “And thy conception”: the labor pains they go through when they bring forth children. “In sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” The sorrow is the menstrual. Keep in mind that Eve is symbolic of the woman, Israel.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

Don't listen to brothers and sisters who make things up, however good the analogy and allegory spoke to your soul, however the beat hit right when the point hit. Don't fall for it.

He came to her, and it was difficult for her to realize he was trying to deceive her and trick her. Its second sense is making use of clever and indirect methods to achieve something. Do you think anything has changed? Some of us say the devil isn't going to get me, I've been doing this too long. The scripture says he is subtil for a reason.

“Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” That was the first deceit. She could have answered, yes, he said we can eat of any tree. The first thing he tries to do is deceive you in your own thoughts: maybe you forgot, maybe you didn't remember.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

points: “We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it.” She caught herself. So the first thing he did was try to confuse her.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

points: “Ye shall not surely die.” Now he is casting doubt: die, what's that? You're not going to die. “For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened.” Sure, you will understand more: you will understand how you are going to die, now that you are going to die as God said. That is the fullness of the understanding he gave her.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

points: He caused confusion, he caused her to doubt, and then he lied to her, and she took and ate. Do we not see that today? All of those things she was supposed to combat, and where was the fight supposed to happen? In her mind. The forefront of the battle takes place in your head, or your heart however you want to see it. We forget that we have all the tools we need right here, and if it doesn't sound right, it isn't right.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

points: “Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field”: this serpent was most subtle, and the class goes to see what it was. “Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” He’s questioning her: God tell you that?
That is twofold. One, he’s the devil, so he’s wiser than everybody there; but it also goes into something more regarding the beasts of the field.

note.label: Good And Evil | Generation To Generation: From Beginning To End

points: “God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.” The tree in the midst of the garden is good and evil. Who taught her that? Adam taught her that.

note.label: Good And Evil | Generation To Generation: From Beginning To End

points: “Ye shall not surely die”: meaning not immediately. He’s playing games with her, semantics.

note.label: Good And Evil | Generation To Generation: From Beginning To End

points: Then he gives her a reason why God told her not to eat of the tree, like a heads up: this is the reason why God said you can’t do it. “Your eyes shall be opened”: you’ll gain wisdom beyond your understanding, you’ll be enlightened. I’m going to tell you what God don’t want you to know.

note.label: Good And Evil | Generation To Generation: From Beginning To End

points: “The tree was good for food”: good to take in, to learn, to apply. “Pleasant to the eyes”: she liked what she saw. “A tree to be desired to make one wise”: to make her wise, to learn what good and evil is. She took of it and did eat, and she brought it to Adam too, “and he did eat.”
The Bible is an abbreviation. It’s not like Eve came to Adam one day and said, let’s be idolaters. It was gradual: hey, I learned something. It took time; it wasn’t immediate.

note.label: Good And Evil | Generation To Generation: From Beginning To End

points: “And the eyes of them both were opened”: both of them gained the enlightenment of what good is and what evil is. “And they knew that they were naked”: they realized, by us doing this we’re sinful, this is wrong. points: Adam and his wife hid themselves “amongst the trees of the garden”: amongst the people.

points: “What is this that thou hast done?” What you do, Eve? “The serpent beguiled me”: the devil did it, he made me do it. Everyone’s pointing fingers at each other.
